transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-09
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Elysian CTO), Jonas Meyer (Lead ML Eng), Priya Rao (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be rough): Quick discovery, customer evaluating Redwood self-serve API to validate latency/cost, wants security paperwork and a short benchmark run to decide hosted vs dedicated.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, with Liam our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:16 Aisha Patel: Good, thanks — we're excited to get a concrete path to first call, we've been reading the docs and want to see the real numbers.
00:32 Liam Ortiz: Awesome. Today we'll aim to get you set up with the self-serve quickstart, hand over some credits, and go over hosting options — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, or Private/VPC. We'll also talk security stuff — SOC2, KMS, SSO.
00:48 Jonas Meyer: Perfect. Our main constraints: sub-200ms P95 for short prompts for interactive features, cost target under $0.001/token-ish for high-volume classification, and data residency for certain datasets.
01:05 Priya Rao: And from infra side we need to know what network changes if we go VPC or on-prem, and whether we can keep logs in our KMS/HSM.
01:22 Maya Chen: Right, makes sense. Quick qualification — what's your current stack? Are you already hitting models anywhere?
01:30 Aisha Patel: We're prototyping on a mix — some in-house distil models for embeddings, and a tiny fleet on OpenAI for chat. We don't want to be locked in though. We want to try Redwood hosted first for speed to value.
01:47 Liam Ortiz: Cool — so self-serve hosted is the fastest. We can spin up API keys right away, give you credits. If you need P95 below 200ms consistently, sometimes customers move to Dedicated for SLAs and reserved throughput. Dedicated also helps with large batch throughput and predictable cost.
02:05 Jonas Meyer: What's the difference in network / data flow between hosted and Private? If we have regulated PII, we might need Private with VPC peering.
02:22 Maya Chen: Hosted keeps model inferencing in our environment — data in flight to Redwood, we retain minimal logs per your retention policy. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and on-prem is fully customer networked. For VPC we can do private endpoints, and you get audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
02:45 Priya Rao: Do you support bring-your-own-KMS or HSM? We have an HSM in Azure.
02:53 Liam Ortiz: Yes, we have KMS integrations, you can bring keys and we integrate with major cloud KMSs. On on-prem we'd do HSM integration as a part of the package.
03:07 Aisha Patel: Ok. For the self-serve, what's the typical time-to-first-token we should expect? From sign up to an actual call.
03:15 Maya Chen: In our PLG flow a median customer sees first successful token in under 20 minutes if they follow the quickstart. For more complex setups with VPC it's usually a few hours to a day. We'll give you a step-by-step.
03:35 Jonas Meyer: Interesting, is the 20 minutes with the default model or with any optimization? Like quantized variants?
03:43 Liam Ortiz: That's with the hosted default model profile — the model catalog has verified performance profiles. If you pick a heavier model you'll see longer latencies, but we also suggest quantized variants and batching configs for lower cost.
04:01 Priya Rao: One of our concerns is the KV cache and prefix caching — we have a couple of reuse patterns, can Redwood preserve session K V cache across requests?
04:15 Liam Ortiz: Yes, KV cache is supported; we call it prefix / KV caching in docs. There's automatic prefix caching and you can pin context to reduce repeated work. Sometimes the docs OCRs it as K V space so apologies for the wording in auto-transcripts.
04:31 Aisha Patel: Ha, okay. Can you walk through the quickstart? We skimmed it but would like the concrete steps.
04:39 Maya Chen: Sure — step 1 sign up and verify org + billingless org to get credits, step 2 get API key, step 3 run the curl example or our SDK snippet, step 4 observe latency in the console and tweak model and batching; we'll send the exact snippet.
05:02 Jonas Meyer: For benchmarking, we want a reproducible script that does 10k short prompts at various concurrencies and records P95, cost per token, and throughput.
05:12 Liam Ortiz: We have a benchmark script — I'll share a python runner that hits the streaming API and a non-streaming path. It captures latency histograms, token counts. We'll also include guidance for setting batching window and suggested hardware if you move to Dedicated.
05:33 Priya Rao: When we run it in our infra, how do we separate customer logs from payloads? We're sensitive about retaining PII.
05:44 Maya Chen: You can configure non-persistence for request payloads on hosted trial, and if you need full separation, Private gives you that. We also support field-level redaction in transit.
06:00 Aisha Patel: Good. Another question — compliance docs. We are SOC2 Type II and need vendor paperwork.
06:09 Maya Chen: We're SOC2 and ISO certs; I'll share the security datasheet and whitepaper, plus our audit contact. Expect a sanitized SOC2 report and the standard security checklist.
06:23 Jonas Meyer: Do you have RBAC that lets us limit access to production keys? We need a separation of duties.
06:31 Liam Ortiz: RBAC is in Console — you can issue tokens with scopes and use token rotation. For Dedicated/Private there's SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning.
06:45 Priya Rao: What about network egress for Private? If we host model inference on dedicated GPUs in our datacenter, is there a traffic pattern we need to plan?
06:55 Liam Ortiz: For on-prem inference, network egress is internal; for VPC we have peering and private link. We'll provide a runbook with ports and subnets to open.
07:10 Aisha Patel: Pricing — our finance team wants rough numbers. Hosted per-token is fine for prototyping, but for scale we want predictable unit economics.
07:21 Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based; we can give you the per-token bands. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with monthly commit and lower unit costs. We can model a hybrid: hosted for low-traffic routes and Dedicated for steady high-volume. We'll send a simple cost model spreadsheet.
07:44 Jonas Meyer: Do you have examples of customers who migrated from hosted to dedicated and what their cost delta looked like?
07:53 Liam Ortiz: Yes, we'll share anonymized examples — typical customer sees 20–40% unit cost reduction with dedicated plus caching and quantization. Exact numbers depend on token distribution and seq lengths.
08:10 Priya Rao: If we want to test an on-prem pilot, how long is the private package provisioning?
08:18 Maya Chen: Private can be a few weeks to provision depending on compliance review; for the pilot we usually do a scoped pilot with a trimmed feature set that can start in 2–4 weeks.
08:33 Aisha Patel: Okay. Let's talk about the runbook for our quick experiment: we want to validate TTFT and cost on the hosted API first. If we hit target numbers we might kick off a Dedicated eval.
08:46 Maya Chen: Totally reasonable. We'll do: grant credits, share benchmark script, and set up a 1-week trial window. If you want we can also give a canary Dedicated quote to show delta.
09:00 Jonas Meyer: One nit — in the SDK examples there's a streaming snippet and a function-calling snippet. Is function calling fully supported in the self-serve?
09:10 Liam Ortiz: Yes, function/tool calling is supported. It's the same API surface; we also support structured output and schema enforcement to reduce hallucinations.
09:23 Priya Rao: Any gotchas with concurrency limits on free credits? We don't want to waste credits by failing early.
09:32 Maya Chen: Free credits have some rate limits to prevent abuse; we'll include those limits in the email. For benchmark runs we'll typically request a temporary raise if needed.
09:45 Aisha Patel: Great. Can you also confirm log retention settings in hosted? We may need 30-day minimum for debugging.
09:52 Liam Ortiz: By default 30 days is fine, but you can configure shorter retention or opt-out of payload retention. For enterprise there's retention export to S3.
10:05 Jonas Meyer: About model variants — you mentioned quantized variants and kernel selection; do we need to change model weights ourselves?
10:14 Liam Ortiz: No, the runtime handles kernel selection and quantized variants are model builds we provide. You choose the variant in the model catalog. For Custom models we can help with compilation and kernel tuning.
10:30 Priya Rao: We're curious about cold NVMe caching for KV — do you recommend SSD-backed caches for large context?
10:38 Liam Ortiz: For very large KV you can use disk-backed caches; we tune caching policy based on sequence lengths and reuse. We'll add our caching doc in the materials.
10:55 Aisha Patel: Ok sounds good. Any security exceptions required for credit access?
11:03 Maya Chen: No exceptions for granting credits for self-serve; for Dedicated/Private there are standard NDAs and paperwork.
11:12 Jonas Meyer: Let's plan an internal test — we'll run the benchmark on Tuesday using the provided script. If numbers look good we'll schedule the dedicated deep dive.
11:24 Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll send the credits and quickstart by tomorrow and Liam will send the benchmark and runbook.
11:32 Priya Rao: About integration — our front end uses streaming to show partial responses. Any suggestions for reducing perceived latency?
11:40 Liam Ortiz: Use the streaming API and smaller model variants; also prefix caching for repeated context helps. On the client side use optimistic UI and socket pooling.
11:55 Aisha Patel: One more — data residency. We have EU-only datasets; can Redwood guarantee region pinning?
12:03 Maya Chen: Yes, we support region pinning for hosted deployments in EU, and Private can be deployed in your region. We'll include regional availability in the security sheet.
12:18 Jonas Meyer: Any hidden per-request charges for function calling or structured outputs?
12:25 Liam Ortiz: No hidden charges beyond token usage and model selection; function calling counts the tokens like any other usage. We'll include cost examples.
12:38 Maya Chen: Alright, quick recap — action items: we give 10k credits, share quickstart sample and benchmark script, send SOC2/security pack, and schedule the dedicated deep-dive. Anything to add?
12:52 Aisha Patel: That covers it. Timing: can you get the materials by end of day tomorrow?
12:59 Maya Chen: Yes — I'll take point on the credits and security pack, Liam on the benchmark.
13:08 Priya Rao: Thanks all, we'll follow up after the bench run.
13:12 Meeting close.
